name: Footer
$status: PROPOSED #261, Dave's eye owed. Nothing in this file is a ruling. A REDESIGN of the PROPOSED #204 build (Lane M, itinerary row 81 'Footer — Incl. doormat / mega-footer'), re-cut at #261 to Dave's scope in his own words: 'App footer for now'. The marketing forms are RETIRED IN THIS FILE, not deleted — see $retired.
purpose: The APP FOOTER: the contentinfo landmark at the bottom of an authenticated application's content column, carrying what an operator needs at the one moment they look down — WHAT AM I LOOKING AT, IS IT REAL, AND HOW OLD IS IT? Product and build identity, the environment badge, data freshness, system status, locale and time zone on the operator's side; privacy, terms, accessibility and support on the regulator's side. One row, inside the content column, never sticky by default.
$redesign-261: ★ THIS COMPONENT ALREADY EXISTED. knowledge/components/footer.meta.json, knowledge/snippets/Footer.reference.html and showroom/footer.html were all built at #204. #261 did not create a component; it re-cut one. What changed, and why, in one place: (1) SCOPE — Dave: 'App footer for now'. The doormat / mega-footer is a marketing and servicing artefact and is out of that scope; it is retired below with its findings preserved so a later marketing pass restores rather than re-derives. (2) TARGETS REVERSED — #204 made every link a 44px target at every width and its own $finding-44px-cost called the height a visible design cost. A one-row app footer cannot pay it: the row would out-grow the app's own toolbar. #261 uses 24px, the ruled dial-down floor (WCAG 2.5.8 AA + the spacing exception), honoured literally with 24px between adjacent link boxes. (3) OPACITY REMOVED — #204 muted its copyright and group headings with alpha-60. MEASURED: #1A1A1A at 0.60 over surface/subtle #F0F0F0 blends to ~#706F6F = 4.41:1, BELOW 4.5, on 12px legal type. Every string is now text/default at full strength; the band is quiet by TYPE SIZE and by 1px cluster pips, not by weakened ink. (4) FOUR THINGS ADDED that only an application footer owes anyone: build identity, environment badge, data freshness, system status.
$vocabularyCollision: ★★ DECLARED BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE AND STILL UNRESOLVED AT #261, because this is the s202-D3 class — the class where Dave rejected a build because one word carried two meanings and every assertion stayed green. In this repo 'footer' ALREADY means the LAYOUT FOOTER of a container: Drawer's footer actions, Modals' dialog footer, Data-grid's pagination footer, Command-palette's hint bar. The gated ACTION-BAR describes itself, verbatim, as 'A footer bar that pins a screen/flow's actions'. This component is the OTHER footer: the document's end matter. THE COLLISION GOT SHARPER AT #261, NOT SOFTER — an app footer and an Action-bar now share a surface, a width and a horizontal one-row shape, and both sit at the bottom of the same screen. They are still not variants: an Action-bar carries the TASK's actions and changes per screen; this carries the SESSION's provenance and does not. ⛔ IF THIS COMPONENT KEEPS THE NAME 'Footer' IT INHERITS THE COLLISION. Renaming is Dave's; nothing here renames anything.

$differsFromNeighbours.Action-bar: See $vocabularyCollision — and read it at #261, because the redesign brought the two shapes closer. Action-bar pins the ACTIONS of a flow, belongs to the task, and its contents change per screen. Footer states the PROVENANCE of the session — which build, which environment, how old the data — and its contents do not change per screen. THE TELL: nothing in a Footer is a thing you do.
$differsFromNeighbours.Status-indicator: Status-indicator owns the dot + label ATOM and this component composes it, form A, unchanged. The Footer is not a status surface: it carries ONE system-level dot as the last of four identity facts, never a per-record status. If the status needs its own row, its own colour ramp or its own history, it is a Banner or a status page, not a footer.
$differsFromNeighbours.Links: Links owns the link ATOM and ships .related, which its own source calls 'the footer / utility pattern'. Footer is the REGION that arranges them: the landmark, the legal row, the rule that separates content from end matter. THE TELL: strip the landmark and the identity cluster and what is left is a .related list, and it should be one.
$differsFromNeighbours.Headers: The masthead sibling. A header carries wayfinding a reader is about to use. An app footer carries the facts a reader needs to trust what the header brought them to — and, unlike a header, it is read only when something looks wrong.
$differsFromNeighbours.Navigations / Sidebar-nav: Those model STATE — current page, expansion, sections, disclosure. An app footer is flat: its only state is the environment and the system status, and both are inputs from the shell, not user state.

props.name: variant
props.$note: default = the full one-row app footer, in document flow at the end of the content column. sticky = the same row pinned to the bottom edge, for a dashboard whose grid genuinely never ends. minimal = version + legal only.

props.name: environment
props.$note: Set as data-env on the footer element; the paint is CSS, so a shell that switches environment cannot forget to restyle anything. prod is a QUIET outlined chip (border/strong + text/default) because production is the normal case and a permanent alarm is no alarm. Every other value takes rag/warning-background with rag/text/on-light ink — 9.16:1, mode-invariant, the ruled 'amber is always black text' pair (R-D3). The label is real text in the markup, never generated content and never an ALL-CAPS run.

props.name: systemStatus
props.$note: Set as data-system. Dot + label, never colour alone (1.4.1); wrapped in role="status" so a degradation announced while the operator is elsewhere on the page is still heard. Only two values by intent: a footer that needs a third has outgrown a footer.

props.name: dataFreshness
props.$note: data-updated (ISO timestamp) plus an optional data-now. Renders an absolute <time> ALWAYS and a relative age as progressive enhancement, with the relative string already present in the markup as the JS-off fallback (s245-D5). data-now is fixed rather than Date.now() so a driven screenshot is byte-deterministic.

props.name: locale
props.$note: Language and time zone as one string ('en-GB · Europe/London (GMT+1)'). It belongs beside the freshness because a timestamp without a zone is not a timestamp — that is the whole reason this pair sits together.

props.name: legalLinks
props.$note: The regulator's row. The list is regulatory, it varies by market, and it is not this file's to fix — see $decisionsForDave 5.

props.name: copyright
props.$note: ADDED #261 Ft3 on Dave's word: 'Be more generous with the spacing and add the copyright notice.' The string is the repo's EXISTING one, unaltered — it already appears verbatim in 17 other snippets — and it is NOT re-typed per surface. It sits at the far right, the last item in the regulator's cluster, and it shares one .ft-end box with the legal links so the two travel together when the row wraps rather than separating across a break. Full ink strength: $finding-opacity-is-not-hierarchy forbids the alpha-60 the #204 build put on exactly this line.

variants.name: default
variants.use: the end of an authenticated application screen — one row inside the content column, in document flow

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: a dashboard whose grid genuinely never ends, where the operator would otherwise never reach the footer. A VARIANT and never the default: a band that follows the operator down costs a row of data on every screen.

variants.name: minimal
variants.use: an embedded, kiosk or single-purpose surface where the operator has no build to report and no data to age — version and legal only

variants.name: doormat
variants.$why: PARKED, NOT RETIRED — s263-D7, Dave at #263: 'park — keep the doormat as a dormant variant of Footer so it stays one component' → 'dormant variant'. Dormant means: declared here, recipe kept whole, NOT built, NOT in any snippet, NOT in the showroom, and NOT reachable from the live variant enum in props[] — the variant prop stays default | sticky | minimal until a marketing pass ships this one. The cost Dave accepted, in his own frame: Footer stays ONE component, at the price of a prop no app footer uses. ⛔ THE FIRST SHAPE OF THIS FILE IS THE FIRST SHAPE OF DORMANT IN THIS REPO — no other components/*.meta.json expresses dormancy (grepped #263, zero hits), so `status: "dormant"` + `why` + `recipe` is the shape offered, not a shape inherited.
variants.use: the marketing / servicing MEGA-FOOTER: the end matter of a marketing or servicing PAGE, not of an authenticated app screen — a banded mat of four named link columns under a brand statement and a back-to-top link, with its own legal bar. PARKED BY s263-D7: it is not shipped in any app footer, and no app surface may reach for it. The full recipe is in `recipe` below, kept verbatim from the #261 retirement note.

$recipe.rehomedAt: #263 — s263-D7, from $retired to this dormant variant

slots.$note: The #261 app footer has NO content slots and that is deliberate — every cluster is a named, typed fact, and a footer with a free slot becomes an Action-bar within one sprint. The #204 'brand' slot (a statement line beside the back-to-top link) is retired with the doormat.

brand.use: the short statement or brand line that opened the mega-footer, beside the back-to-top link

tokens.surface: surface/subtle — the app-shell rows in the specimen. ⛔ NO LONGER THE FOOTER BAND: see $reversedOutBand.
tokens.divider: divider/border/section — the app-shell rules in the specimen. ⛔ NO LONGER THE FOOTER'S TOP RULE: the rule is GONE (#261 Ft3).
tokens.$pipsTakeTheSectionRule: MEASURED AND CORRECTED TWICE. First: the pips were divider/border/subsection, which resolves to #F0F0F0 in light — the old surface/subtle band — and were invisible; they moved to divider/border/section. Then #261 Ft3 reversed the band out, and the section rule went invisible in the other direction. They now take border/strong (#808080 both modes), the one neutral that holds its edge on BOTH plates: 4.41:1 on #1A1A1A, 3.79:1 on #FAFAFA. divider/border/subsection has no consumer in this component.
tokens.text: text/default — EVERY string, at full strength; there is no muted text in this component
tokens.border-strong: border/strong — the production environment chip outline
tokens.env-alert-ink: rag/text/on-light — amber is ALWAYS black text (R-D3), 9.16:1, mode-invariant
tokens.radius: border-radius/control — the link focus shape and the environment chip; both square
tokens.target: target/min (44px) — bound so the drift gate reads the ruled default, though the LINKS use the 24px floor
tokens.$rag: PRESENT AT #261, and this is a change from #204 which declared RAG absent. Two roles only, both status-of-the-SYSTEM and never status-of-a-record: the environment chip fill (rag/warning-background, the salience-ramp fill rung with its ruled black ink) and the system dot (rag/success-glyph / rag/warning-glyph). No error red appears anywhere in this component — an outage is a Banner, not a footer pip.
tokens.$notATokenTargetFloor: ⚠ --target-floor:24px IS DECLARED IN CSS AND DELIBERATELY ABSENT FROM THE MANIFEST. 24 is the ruled dial-down hit-area floor, named verbatim in tokens/layout.json target.$description — 'Dial-down floor is 24 (WCAG 2.5.8 AA + spacing exception); never below' — but the store carries NO LEAF for it: only target/min (44px) exists. Rather than invent a token in a shared file outside the lane fence, or bind a 44px token to a 24px box and lie to the drift gate, the value is declared locally with this note. Minting target/floor is $decisionsForDave 1.
tokens.ft-band: surface/action-primary — THE REVERSED-OUT PLATE. #1A1A1A light / #FAFAFA dark; supercharge warms it to #13110E / #F0EFED through the ADR-0014 ramp, driven and confirmed.
tokens.ft-ink: text/on-inverse — the plate's ink. #FFFFFF light (17.4:1) / #333333 dark (12.0:1). Its own $note defines it as the 'Label for surfaces whose lightness INVERTS between modes', which is exactly this seat.
tokens.$reversedOutBand: #261 Ft3. DAVE, VERBATIM: 'The footer should be reversed out in both light and dark. Do we have reversed-out tokens, a modifier for light mode?' ANSWER, both halves. (1) TOKENS: YES. surface/action-primary + text/on-inverse is the design system's inverse pair — the Mono primary-button plate — and it is the ONLY semantic surface whose lightness inverts between modes. Nothing was minted and no hex was invented. (2) A LIGHT-MODE MODIFIER: NO. There is no inverse/hero SURFACE ROLE, and its absence is already a logged gap: knowledge/_COMPONENT-GAPS.md row 'Inverse / hero surface', opened 2026-06-30, verbatim 'no light-mode dark-band role', whose proposed fix is to promote a semantic inverse/surface ramp. This component therefore COMPOSES the modifier locally from the two ruled tokens (--ft-band / --ft-ink) and FLAGS it here rather than promoting a role, which is Dave's to rule. The gap row's named failure is a component inventing a charcoal (#0E1014); this one does not. ⚠ WHAT DAVE SHOULD LOOK AT BEFORE HE RULES: a true inverse plate in DARK mode is a LIGHT band (#FAFAFA) under a #1A1A1A page — that is what 'reversed out in both' means and it is drawn honestly. If he wants the dark-mode band quieter the softer ruled pair is surface/action + text/reverse-secondary (#626262/#FFF light 6.1:1, #808080/#1A1A1A dark 5.32:1), one token swap, same shape.
tokens.$dotRing: #261 Ft3: the status dot gained a 1px border/strong ring. It is not decoration-for-decoration's-sake — the RAG glyphs are MODE-INVARIANT by s122-D2 (#66CC8D / #E0A61F in both modes), so on the DARK-MODE plate (#FAFAFA, a LIGHT ground) the green dot alone measures ~1.9:1 and disappears. The dot remains decoration and the label still carries the meaning (1.4.1); a decoration you cannot see is simply not there.
tokens.$twoRedLawOnAnInverseSurface: s151-D1 on this component: there is NO red text seat — no plus/minus numerals, no error string — and the only coloured marks are RAG dot fills, mode-invariant by s122-D2. Recorded because the law INVERTS on a reversed-out plate and the next author will need it: the red is keyed to the GROUND, not the mode, so a red here would be #F6604C on the light-mode plate (a dark ground) and #DA1A00 on the dark-mode plate (a light ground) — the opposite of the usual mapping. Nothing in the shipped file paints one.

$finding-24px-floor: ★ THE APP FOOTER IS THE FIRST COMPONENT TO NEED THE DIAL-DOWN FLOOR AS A TOKEN, AND IT ISN'T ONE. The 44px standard is a hit-area guarantee for CONTROLS, and it is right for them. It is wrong for a one-row footer: four legal links at 44px make a 44px band, taller than the app toolbar above it, for the least-used links on the screen. The ruled floor of 24 exists precisely for this case and the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception is honoured literally here (24px of gap between adjacent 24px boxes, so no two targets are ever closer than 24px). But the floor lives only in a $description string, so every component that needs it must hardcode it and declare it, as this one does. MEASURED consequence of the alternative: a 44px footer is 40px taller than the shipped one, per screen, forever.
$finding-opacity-is-not-hierarchy: ★ MEASURED, AND IT REVERSES THE PREVIOUS BUILD. #204 muted its copyright line and group headings with opacity:var(--alpha-60). Composited: #1A1A1A at 0.60 over surface/subtle #F0F0F0 = ~#706F6F, which is 4.41:1 against that ground — below the 4.5 text threshold, on 12px legal type. NO GATE CAUGHT IT, because the snippet gate reads the DECLARED contrast pairs and the declared pair was text/default on surface/subtle at full strength, which passes. Opacity is invisible to the pair check. The fix is not a bigger alpha; it is that an app footer has no muted text at all — hierarchy comes from type size (12px legal against 14px product) and from the 1px pips between clusters. Generalisable: ⛔ AN ALPHA APPLIED TO A TEXT ELEMENT DEFEATS THE CONTRAST GATE SILENTLY. That is a gate gap, reported, not a footer problem.
$finding-type-debt-conflict: ★★ CARRIED FORWARD FROM #204, STILL GOVERNING. 'COPY THE APPROVED ARTEFACT VERBATIM' AND 'ADD ZERO TO THE SHRINK-ONLY TYPE RATCHET' CONFLICT WHEN THE APPROVED ARTEFACT IS ITSELF IN DEBT. The gated Links atom writes font-weight:500 twice in its own CSS — on a.arrow and on a.lnk[aria-current="page"] — and those are exactly the raw declarations TYPE-002 counts. Copying them verbatim DROVE _validate_type_composites.py red on this file at #204 (measured: 2 violations). The emphasis therefore arrives through canon/type.css's own .em modifier applied in the MARKUP (the T-D14 markup-class route): identical rendered weight, zero added debt. Links itself was NOT edited — it is a gated shared artefact and its two declarations are the BUILD-PM's to retire. THE DIVERGENCE FROM THE PARENT IS DECLARED, NOT HIDDEN.

accessibility.landmark: <footer role="contentinfo"> with aria-label="Application footer", so a screen on which an Action-bar or a Data-grid pagination row also renders does not present two anonymous contentinfo regions.
accessibility.grouping: The legal links are a <nav aria-label="Legal and support">. The identity and provenance clusters are NOT navigation and are not marked as such — four facts are not a landmark.
accessibility.systemStatus: role="status" on the dot+label pair, so a degradation that appears while the operator is elsewhere on the page is announced. The dot is aria-hidden; the LABEL carries the meaning (1.4.1).
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: The environment is a word before it is a colour ('Production' / 'User acceptance testing'). The system status is a sentence before it is a dot. Links are underlined, never distinguished by colour.
accessibility.targetSize: Legal links are 24px — the ruled dial-down floor — with 24px of gap between adjacent boxes, which is the WCAG 2.5.8 AA spacing exception honoured literally rather than cited. NOT 44px, and that is a deliberate reversal of the #204 position: see $finding-24px-floor.
accessibility.declaredAbsence: THE STATUS DOT'S OWN CONTRAST IS A DECLARED ABSENCE, on the Status-indicator precedent whose meta already records that the amber dot is below 3:1 standalone. It is decoration; the label is the accessibility channel. The environment chip is NOT an absence — its ink is a gated pair at 9.16:1.
accessibility.linkText: Every link names its destination. No 'click here', no 'more', no 'read more' — the aca-004 class the snippet gate blocks.

antiPatterns: Never make the app footer sticky by default. A band that follows the operator down an infinite grid costs a row of data on every screen; sticky is a variant, chosen, for the dashboard that genuinely never ends.
Never put the primary task's actions in a Footer. That is an Action-bar, and at #261 the two shapes are close enough that the mistake is easy — the test is whether the thing is something you DO.

Never leave the environment badge off a non-production build. Acting on user-acceptance data believing it is production is the single most expensive mistake a banking console permits, and this badge is the cheapest guard against it.
Never show a timestamp without its time zone. A freshness figure with no zone is not a fact; that is why locale and time zone sit in the same cluster.
Never mute footer text with opacity. It defeats the contrast gate silently — MEASURED at 4.41:1 in the previous build. Quietness comes from type size.
Never let the system dot carry a per-record status, a third colour or a history. One system-level fact, two values; anything more is a Banner or a status page.
Never ship an anonymous <footer> on a screen that also has a container footer — a screen-reader user then has two contentinfo regions and no way to tell them apart.
Never carry legal text as an image or a PDF-only link with no text alternative in the bar itself.
REVIEW Never promote, gate or register this component without Dave's word. It is PROPOSED #261, and the name, the 24px floor and the RAG-in-a-footer position are all open.

responsive.wrap: RE-MEASURED #261 Ft3 in Chromium with the full content (the copyright notice now included): default = ONE 56px row at 1600px of viewport and above; TWO rows, 92px, at 1440/1280/1024; THREE rows, 128px, at 768; a stack at 375, 228px. Sticky is 56 and minimal 48 down to 768. EVERY height at EVERY width is a multiple of 4 — driven, not claimed (notes/_lanes/261Ft3/_w2.py). ⚠ THE ONE-ROW WIDTH MOVED FROM 1440 TO 1600 and that is the price of Dave's copyright notice: the right-hand cluster grew by ~200px. Below a 640px CONTAINER width the legal/copyright cluster is forced onto its own line; everything above is natural flex wrap. A CONTAINER query, so a footer in a narrow split pane wraps on a 27-inch monitor — which is the point. The provenance cluster is flex:0 1 auto, not 1 1 auto: MEASURED, a growing cluster ate 995px of a 1600px row and pushed the legal links onto a second line at every width.
responsive.stack: Below a 375px CONTAINER everything stacks to a column and EVERY pip is removed (not just the ones inside the provenance cluster), because a vertical 1px rule between stacked rows reads as a divider rather than a separator. Every stacked leaf keeps the 24px seat, so the stack lands on the grid at 228 rather than collapsing to 10.48px line boxes.
responsive.targets: MEASURED at 1600 / 1440 / 1280 / 1024 / 768 / 420 / 375: link height 24px and minimum gap between adjacent link boxes 24px at EVERY one. An earlier cut tightened the stacked gap to 16px, which broke the 2.5.8 spacing exception the whole 24px position rests on; it was measured, caught and reverted.
responsive.$bentoNote: s248-D3 — an edit mode is coming and every component placed in a bento tile must be responsive. This one is container-queried end to end and carries no viewport media query at all.

dimensions.$note: #261 Ft3, DAVE'S WORDS: 'One 41px row — I should never see a figure like 41, we have a 4px grid.' 41 was rowMinHeight 40 + a 1px border-top. The border-top is GONE (the reversed-out plate separates itself from the page by value, so the rule had no work left to do) and every figure here is a multiple of 4. MEASURED IN CHROMIUM at 1920/1600/1440/1280/1024/768/375 and across 4 themes x 2 modes on the showroom page: default 56 one-row (>=1600 of viewport, i.e. >=1558 of container), 92 two-row, 128 three-row at 768, 228 stacked at 375; sticky 56; minimal 48. EVERY height at EVERY width is a multiple of 4 — that is now a driven assertion, not a claim (notes/_lanes/261Ft3/_w2.py). Two mechanisms hold it: min-height 56/48 on .ft-inner (box-sizing is border-box, so the figure INCLUDES the padding and is the figure on the tape), and a 24px min-height on every cluster and, in the 375 stack, on every leaf — without the second one a wrapped line collapsed to a 10.48px line box and put 78.48 on the tape. The 1px pip WIDTH and the 1px chip border are hairlines, not spacing: they are the only non-multiples left. linkMinHeight 24 and linkGap 24 remain the ruled dial-down floor plus the 2.5.8 spacing exception. There is NO innerMaxWidth: the app footer takes the width of the shell's content column and centring is the shell's job — the change from the #204 doormat's 1120px rail. ONE ROW IS NO LONGER FREE AT 1440: the copyright notice Dave asked for costs ~200px on the right, so 1440 wraps to two rows and 1600+ stays one. Reported, not hidden.

$decisionsForDave: 1 · MINT target/floor = 24px? The dial-down floor is RULED and is named verbatim in tokens/layout.json's target $description, but it has no leaf token, so this component hardcodes 24 and declares it. Every future dense component will do the same. Mint it, or keep the floor as prose?

2 · THE NAME, STILL.
